grammar.title: Hear the regional copula in an ordinary chat
grammar.formation: Noun / na-adjective stem + や; past やった; explanatory noun + なんや, verb clause + んや. Do not attach copula や directly to a plain verb or i-adjective.
grammar.explanation: Tamura uses や where the corresponding standard casual copula is だ. そや is agreement, and ほんまや responds to something just noticed. Here the words belong to friendly off-duty conversation. A speaker can also use standard polite language in a business call. Learn the sentence meaning first, without assuming every Kansai speaker chooses identical endings.
grammar.translation: This is a shop I often go to.

examples.ja: ここ、{行|い}きつけの{店|みせ}や。
examples.en: This is a shop I often go to.

examples.ja: あの{湯飲|ゆの}み、{先生|せんせい}のお{気|き}に{入|い}りやったな。
examples.en: That cup was the teacher’s favourite, wasn’t it?

examples.ja: ほんまや。{紙袋|かみぶくろ}が{濡|ぬ}れてる。
examples.en: You’re right. The paper bag’s wet.

grammar.mistake: Recognise や as a copula here, not the standard list particle in パンやお茶. ほんまや is not a rule that i-adjectives take や.

grammar.title: Recognise the negative before judging the plan
grammar.formation: Selected forms here: 食べる → 食べへん; 分かる → 分からへん; 足りる → 足りへん; 濡れる → 濡れへん. Regional and individual alternatives exist.
grammar.explanation: へん makes the selected verbs negative: 食べへん is not eat, not an extra positive action. Tamura declines a taste so eight purchased cakes remain eight. Recognise the whole form in its situation. Godan stems and short verbs have regional variants; some surface forms can overlap potential forms. This lesson does not ask you to derive every verb with one universal stem rule.
grammar.example: 今は食べへん。会場で食べる。
grammar.translation: I won’t eat one now. I’ll have it at the venue.

examples.ja: {今|いま}は{食|た}べへん。{会場|かいじょう}で{食|た}べる。
examples.en: I won’t eat one now. I’ll have it at the venue.

examples.ja: これだけやと、{人数|にんずう}が{分|わ}からへん。
examples.en: From this alone, I can’t tell how many people there are.

examples.ja: {棚|たな}の{上|うえ}なら{紙袋|かみぶくろ}は{濡|ぬ}れへん。
examples.en: On top of the shelf, the paper bag won’t get wet.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate every regional e-stem + へん as can’t: form and meaning vary by area and context. Here eight minus one would not be enough, so 足りへん refers to a shortage.

grammar.title: Follow everyday regional words through the situation
grammar.formation: めっちゃ + description; ほんま / ほんまに; なんぼ in a price question; おおきに for thanks; ほな as then; あかん with the surrounding action.
grammar.explanation: めっちゃ intensifies a description; ほんま responds to truth or surprise; なんぼ asks a price here. おおきに thanks Mori for carrying a bag, not a greeting. ほな moves to the next step. In ここに置いたらあかん？, Tamura asks whether putting the bag there is a bad idea. Context supplies the force. These words do not by themselves identify a stranger’s origin or make a sentence formally polite.
grammar.example: これ、なんぼ？二百円？めっちゃ安いな。
grammar.translation: How much is this? Two hundred yen? That’s really cheap.

examples.ja: これ、なんぼ？{二百円|にひゃくえん}？めっちゃ{安|やす}いな。
examples.en: How much is this? Two hundred yen? That’s really cheap.

examples.ja: {紙袋|かみぶくろ}、{持|も}ってくれておおきに。
examples.en: Thanks for carrying the paper bag.

examples.ja: ここに{置|お}いたらあかん？ほな、{棚|たな}に{置|お}くわ。
examples.en: Shouldn’t I put it here? Then I’ll put it on the shelf.

grammar.mistake: あかん can judge something as no good or disallow an action; use the actual sentence. めっちゃ is casual emphasis, not a dependable geographical label.

grammar.title: Follow whose action receives regional respect
grammar.formation: Selected recognition forms: 来る → きはる; 使う → 使いはる; 待っている → 待ってはる. Godan attachment and ongoing forms differ across regions.
grammar.explanation: Tamura refers to Satō-sensei’s arrival, cup choice and waiting with はる. Respect concerns the person doing the action, not simply who hears the sentence. The tone can remain friendly. Regional use is broader than standard formal honorifics and varies with relationships; this is not a universal substitute for workplace keigo. Focus on the doer and the action in these lines, with 来る written きはる to make the reading explicit.
grammar.example: 先生は三時半にきはる。
grammar.translation: The teacher is coming at half past three.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{三時半|さんじはん}にきはる。
examples.en: The teacher is coming at half past three.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}、この{湯飲|ゆの}みを{使|つか}いはるかな。
examples.en: I wonder whether the teacher will use this cup.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}が{店先|みせさき}で{待|ま}ってはる。
examples.en: The teacher’s waiting outside the shop.

grammar.mistake: The teacher performs these actions. Do not choose Mori merely because Mori hears the line, or derive all regional はる forms from the standard masu stem.

dialogues.title: Eight cakes, not seven
dialogues.description: On Saturday morning, Tamura and Mori stop at Tamura’s regular bakery to buy sweets for their community film gathering.

lines.line: ここ、よく{来|く}るの？

lines.meaning: Do you come here often?

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: そや。{行|い}きつけの{店|みせ}や。{今日|きょう}は{焼|や}きたてやな。
lines.romaji: So ya. Ikitsuke no mise ya. Kyō wa yakitate ya na.
lines.meaning: Yeah. It’s a shop I often go to. They’re freshly baked today.

lines.romaji: Ii nioi. Jōei no ato ni taberu bun, hakko kaō ka.

lines.speaker: Tamura
lines.line: うん。これ、なんぼ？

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {一個|いっこ}{二百円|にひゃくえん}だって。

lines.speaker: Mori

lines.speaker: Tamura

lines.speaker: Mori

dialogues.title: A smaller cup, a dry bag

exercises.prompt: Why does Tamura know this shop?
options: It is a shop Tamura often visits
exercises.explain: 行きつけの店 means a shop one regularly visits; ownership is not stated.

exercises.prompt: What price does Mori give for one cake?
exercises.explain: 一個二百円 is the unit price; eight is the chosen quantity.

exercises.prompt: Why does Tamura refuse to taste one now?
options: It would leave only seven of the eight they need
exercises.explain: Tamura says 足りへん: eight minus one would leave them short. There is no dislike or shop rule.
店や is the copula after the noun, corresponding to standard casual 店だ.
exercises.line: ここ、{行|い}きつけの{店|みせ}＿＿。
exercises.context: Recover Tamura’s regional copula after a noun: ここ、行きつけの店＿＿。

exercises.prompt: Read 今は食べへん。会場で食べる。 Which meaning fits?
options: I won’t eat now; I’ll eat at the venue
I have already eaten at the venue
I won’t eat at the venue either
exercises.explain: へん negates the first action only. The second sentence says the later eating will happen.
exercises.line: {今|いま}は{食|た}べへん。{会場|かいじょう}で{食|た}べる。

exercises.prompt: Mori offers to carry the bag. What does Tamura’s おおきに do here?
options: Ask how much the bag costs
exercises.explain: It responds to the offer with thanks. The preceding action identifies its function.

exercises.meaning: Constrained recall: this cake smells really fragrant.
exercises.explain: めっちゃ intensifies 香ばしい. The tiles practise this supplied sentence, not free dialect production.

exercises.prompt: Why is Tamura glad they stopped by in the morning?
options: The cakes can sell out by midday
The screening begins in the morning
exercises.explain: The message says 昼には売り切れになることもある. The film starts at four.

exercises.prompt: Why will they wait until after the film to open the bag?
options: Rustling could make the recorded voice hard to hear
The bag belongs to the teacher
The cakes must be baked again
exercises.explain: がさがさ音がして声が聞こえへん is a listening problem caused by the rustling bag.

exercises.prompt: What would make them skip the stop to look at the shop photo?
options: The teacher uses a smaller cup
exercises.explain: If the train time is near, they will go directly to the station. The detour is conditional, not cancelled already.

exercises.prompt: What arrival time does Tamura report for the teacher?
exercises.explain: 三時半にきはる gives the teacher’s arrival. It is not the four-o’clock film start.

exercises.prompt: What does Mori say about the old cup?
options: One broke; a smaller one is available
It is too expensive to use
The teacher has taken every cup home
exercises.explain: 一つ割れちゃって reports the break. 小さいのならある offers the available alternative.

exercises.prompt: Why does Mori suggest putting the bag on the shelf?
options: Steam would make it wet in the first spot
The shelf is where the teacher always sits
exercises.explain: Mori names the steam risk and then suggests the shelf; Tamura accepts the dry alternative.

exercises.prompt: Whose waiting receives the respectful はる form in this sentence?
exercises.explain: 先生が names the doer. This is an explicit subject question, not guessing a person from an accent.
exercises.line: {先生|せんせい}が{店先|みせさき}で{待|ま}ってはる。

options: The teacher is coming at half past three
exercises.explain: きはる is the selected respectful regional form of 来る; the teacher is the subject.
exercises.line: {先生|せんせい}は{三時半|さんじはん}にきはる。

exercises.meaning: Constrained recognition/recall: I wonder if the teacher will use this cup.
exercises.explain: The teacher is the doer and かな leaves the choice uncertain; it does not say the cup has been chosen already.

exercises.prompt: Who suggested tasting a cake, and who declined?
options: The teacher suggested it; both declined
exercises.explain: The diary’s 私 is Mori. Tamura responds 今は食べへん. Keep narrator and quoted speaker separate.

exercises.prompt: What did Mori do after Tamura noticed the teacher outside?
options: Sent the teacher to the station
Started the film without the teacher
exercises.explain: Tamura reports the waiting; Mori then guides the teacher in. Mori is not the waiting teacher.

exercises.prompt: What happened to the smaller cup by the end of the diary?
exercises.explain: The earlier dialogue asks 使いはるかな, an open possibility; the later diary reports actual use.

exercises.prompt: How many cakes remained after the tea break?
options: Seven, because Tamura ate one early
exercises.explain: 八個ともなくなった means all eight were gone. Tamura had declined the early taste.
